text:
Ada: heads-up — seeing persistent mem growth on a few long-context sessions after the kernel-selection changes. looks like the KV cache is leaving tiny unreachable fragments (weird small slabs)
Josh: can you paste a sample of the slab histogram / growth numbers?
Ada: yep. grabbed from a repro run: 
```
Ada:  kv_slab_total: 12.1GB
Ada:  kv_slab_free_small: 420MB
Ada:  kv_slab_fragments_count: 13472
Ada:  avg_fragment_size: 28 bytes
Ada:  growth_after_100k_tokens: +1.9GB
```
Priya: avg fragment 28 bytes... that smells like internal allocator rounding to small block buckets. are we splitting large slots into tiny leftovers?
Marta: more context — this started after we switched the kernel selector to favor RTX precompiled kernels for long seqs. those kernels change packing patterns (different KV write sizes). could be an allocator mismatch.
Sam: also noticed batching heuristics now produce slightly larger KV write bursts which could increase free-list churn.
Josh: hmm. two hypotheses: (1) allocator bucket granularity too coarse vs actual write sizes => internal slack, (2) fragmentation from partial evictions + pinned KV refs for long contexts.
Ada: i instrumented alloc/free heatmap. attached snippet: 
```
Ada:  heatmap sample (older run): buckets: [16,32,64,128,256]
Ada:  heatmap sample (new run): buckets: [24,40,80,160]  <-- non-power-of-two alignment
```
Priya: non-power-of-two alignment is suspect. our allocator assumes power-of-two classing for quick coalescing. if kernels emit 24-byte frames repeatedly we get >1 fragment per frame.
Marta: idea: add a 'mini-compact' pass that runs opportunistically on low-cpu cores and merges adjacent tiny fragments into intermediate blocks. budget it tightly.
Josh: how would mini-compact decide which slabs to touch? we need a heuristic that doesn't thrash. maybe target slabs with high fragment density and low live object density.
Priya: +1. score slab by (fragmented_bytes / slab_size) * (1 - live_ratio). thresholds: score>0.25 and free_bytes>64KB then compact.
Sam: we should also consider async copying vs in-place compaction. copying has CPU cost but avoids stop-the-world. copying can be paused/resumed to avoid latency spikes.
Ada: latency impact is a concern. requests hitting the same GPU must not see >5ms p99 regression. we can throttle compaction to spare cycles between batches.
Marta: another angle: change blocksize tuning in the kernel-compile path so emitted KV frames align to allocator classes. cheaper: pad writes to nearest class for longer seq kernels.
Josh: padding seems low-effort but increases token bytes. tradeoff: slight memory overhead vs avoiding thousands of tiny fragments. need experiments.
Priya: we can simulate both: (A) miner compact with tight budget, (B) pad writes to nearest 32-byte class. measure mem-growth after 200k tokens and p50/p99 latencies.
Sam: i'll add a small perf test harness: single GPU, emulate long chat with 500k tokens, both old and new kernel selectors + padding toggles.
Ada: infra-bot: can you spin a canary with the compaction hook disabled/enabled and attach trace ids?
infra-bot: created canary runs: run/3642007901 (compact-off), run/3642007912 (compact-on), run/3642007923 (padding-on). logs will be in /runs/36420079xx by EOD. :robot_face:
Josh: nice. also let's capture live fragmentation map every 10k tokens so we can correlate with batching bursts.
Priya: if mini-compact helps, we should expose a runtime flag per-deployment: compact_budget_ms_per_minute, and a slab_score_threshold. ops teams can tune per workload.
Marta: note: compaction might interact with batching heuristics — if we compact during a peak, we'll reduce available free KV and batching may shrink which could hurt throughput. need to coordinate with batching controller.
Sam: propose adding a simple handshake: batching controller publishes 'window_idle' signal; compactor only runs if window_idle>100ms. cheap and effective.
Ada: action items:
Ada:  - Sam: add harness + frag sampling (ETA 2d)
Ada:  - Josh: prototype mini-compact & slab scoring (ETA 3d)
Ada:  - Priya: experiment padding write to 32B classes, measure memory overhead (ETA 2d)
Ada:  - Marta: check kernel compile path for alignment knobs + coordinate with runtime (ETA 2d)
Ada:  - infra-bot: run canaries and post logs (ETA end of day)

Josh: one more: collect kernel-level metrics to see how many writes are 24/40/80 bytes — that'll confirm root cause.
Priya: noted. i'll add counters in the write path and histogram export.
Marta: ok team, let's reconvene after initial runs. if we see >50% reduction in fragment_count with padding + no latency regression, we can ship padding first while we refine compactor. :shipit: 
Sam: 👍
Ada: thanks all. I'll open RFC for mini-compact once Josh has a prototype.
